entries.creator: Michaeeas
entries.attribution: "Yi Action Camera" by Michaeeas is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0), via Wikimedia Commons. Cropped and resized.
entries.confidence_reason: All six hard rules clearly hold, the background is plain and neutral, and the framing is a clean three-quarter view from above. The item is unmistakably a compact boxy action camera: wide-angle lens, power button, mode icons, tripod socket and textured grip panels. It is the only subject and fills most of the square. No people or hands appear. I zoomed into the top face, both side faces and the lens at close to native resolution and found no readable brand, logo or model text. The only markings are a power symbol and small video/photo pictograms, and the side panels have a decorative brick-line texture with no letters. There is no watermark, overlaid text, border or collage. The crop is 1700px (left 100, top 60, which fits inside 1920x1920), well above 800. One minor point: the camera lies with its lens pointing up rather than facing the viewer, which is a little unusual. It still reads immediately as an action camera, so I did not downgrade.
entries.alt_text: White compact action camera with a black wide-angle lens on a plain white background

entries.confidence_reason: I tried to refute the pick and could not. Every hard rule clearly holds. The crop shows one leather wallet, closed and seen straight-on from the front, centred on a plain white background. It fills about 85% of the width, with even margins on every side. There are no people, hands, logos, text, watermarks or borders. The square is 1454px of source pixels, well above 800. The item type is confirmed by the open-view photos of the same object (candidates 47, 48 and 50), which show bill and card pockets. The only caveat is appearance: this is a worn vintage museum piece with a faded, greyish flap.

entries.confidence_reason: I could not refute any hard rule. The background is a plain white studio sweep, the three-quarter framing is good, and the whole product fits inside the 1500px square with margin on every side. Two doubts keep this below high. First, the product is an unusual armless design: a cord replaces the temple arms, so it is less typical than a classic pair. Second, the word "OMBRAZ" is faintly printed at the top edge of the upper lens and can just be made out at source resolution with 8x zoom. In the 800px crop it is a smudge about 35px wide and cannot be read, even contrast-normalised at 12x.
